title: Lived-In Light — Candid Home Tour Opener
description: A full-bleed candid interior photograph does all the heavy lifting here, with italic caption, small-cap city tag, and owner byline tucked quietly into the lower quarter — never competing with the image, always subordinate to it.
philosophy: This template is built on the conviction that the photograph already contains the story, and type's only job is a soft, unhurried footnote. It refuses styled studio compositions, high-contrast headline hierarchies, and anything that signals corporate polish. The speaker using it is handing the audience a room to inhabit, not a deck to read. Restraint here is not minimalism — it is editorial trust.
goodFor: Home tour and living-space editorial openers
3-line italic pull captions anchored beneath full-bleed photography
Interior design or architecture portfolio presentations
Cultural magazine pitches where image narrative leads and copy follows
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly business reviews requiring structured data layout
Product launch decks needing dominant headline hierarchy
Any slide where the photograph is decorative rather than the primary content
Conference talks requiring high-contrast legibility in bright projection rooms
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide should feel like pausing on the opening spread of a Sunday supplement — unhurried, warm, confident that the photograph is enough. Compositionally asymmetric: the image breathes at full scale while the type cluster in the lower-left acts as a soft annotation, never a headline. Mood is late-afternoon domestic light — candid, unlabored, never staged. Avoid any graphic device that signals 'presentation': no bold hierarchies, no structural chrome, nothing that belongs in a boardroom.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed photograph bleeds to all four edges with zero margin — the image is the entire slide surface. A gentle gradient scrim rises from the bottom edge across the lower 22% of the canvas, carving a quiet caption zone without competing with the image. Text lives on a 12-column grid: the italic title and small-cap location tag sit left-aligned in cols 2–8, while the owner byline anchors to col 2 at roughly 4% from the lower edge. No header band, no page number, no decorative rule — only the photograph and its understated footnote cluster.

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like a page torn from a slow Sunday supplement — warm ambient light pools unevenly across the room, the camera caught something unstaged. Compositionally the image is the entire argument; the lower text band is a hushed editorial footnote, present but never asserting. Rhythm is deliberately asymmetric: visual weight saturates the upper two-thirds while the caption zone is spare and almost apologetic in its footprint. Avoid anything that signals curation or graphic intervention — no vignettes with hard edges, no overlay boxes, no treatment that makes the photograph feel art-directed after the fact.
